author: Claude Opus 5.5 (engineering lead) with Claude Sonnet 5.5 (cand-a v4 implementation agent)
summary: Hexagonal-prism tumbler, version 4: one rigid hexagonal body (circumradius 25.5 mm) that rolls over its hexagon edges onto face F3 (rest orientation 180 deg about y, lobe parked at body -z), driven by an internal lift ring with one lobe (geared from a 6 mm gearmotor, 304 internal-gear band in a PA12 carrier); axial couplers on the two end faces: a machined 304 hex peg on the head (6.5 mm engagement), and a tail receiver with a roll-in channel re-derived from the corrected roll kinematics (two arcs through the F3 bottom vertices), a yaw turntable, a flat 304 seat and 304 three-flat jaw roll lock, a 304 thrust washer, and a motor-driven over-centre four-bar keeper with an outrigger bushing (third gearmotor, no SMA, no spring). BLE only, no power transfer.

components.description: tail receiver cap half l (PA12, y -12.0 to -7.0). assembly_access.statement: Walls and end plates are separate PA12 parts joined by two PA12 axial posts (from y -6.9 to the head end plate) and four M1.6 screws (screw positions are a lumped stand-in). The V-shaped roll-in channel cuts end plate b and the tail cap into three pieces that are each fixed to the wall ring and to the cap strips by the thrust washer and screws (not designed). Each wall half (head and tail) is a separate part so the lift ring can be dropped into the girdle slot between them. The cell, controller and boards load as a stack along the axis with one end plate removed; the head peg installs from the head end plate and the tail receiver parts (puck, seat web with thrust washer, keeper tongue, jaw and rod) install from the tail end. M3 is a column in the vacated left interior slot with its outrigger post standing on end plate b; M2 is the right interior column. No assembly sequence has been verified; the gear train, yaw worm, four-bar routing and the press fits are not shown to be assemblable.

coupler_sites.mount: datum on the head peg axis where a neighbour's tail face sits when docked (gap g = 8 mm from the head end face at y = 14 mm, 5 mm peg engagement)
tail receiver on end plate b (tail face)

retention.mechanism: The head peg's annular groove (dia 3.0 x 1.4 wide, groove centre at A-frame y 27.1 = 5.1 mm inside the neighbour's face; engagement 6.5 mm, tip y 28.5) is closed from above (body +z) by a 1.0 mm 304 keeper tongue (B frame y -9.4 to -8.4) whose closed lower edge is on the peg axis (z 0.0) with a semicircular notch r 1.55 that rests on the upper half of the groove root (dia 3.0). Groove engagement: the tongue overlaps the upper half of the peg shoulder between the groove root (r 1.5) and the hex, area 3.39 mm2 (v3: 1.5 mm2 as two prongs). Tension path (design tension 4 mu W = 1.637 N, mu 1 provisional): peg tip-side shoulder, tongue, stem (2 x 2) in the PA12 guide slot of the puck column, puck web (y -7.0 to -4.4), 304 thrust washer (flat thrust face, 7.6 mm2 bearing on the cap strips), cap strips, tail wall ring. The tongue is moved by a motor-driven over-centre four-bar: crank r 2.0 on the M3 axis (-4.500, 12.272), link 10.216 mm, rocker pivot (5.250, 15.322) (link-side arm 3.0, output arm 4.5), push rod on the yaw axis through the hollow yaw shaft, pin-in-slot yoke bar. Two stable geometric states: CLOSED = crank 10 deg past the folded dead centre against a hard stop, OPEN = 10 deg past the extended dead centre against a second stop (the crank travels 202.5 deg, the rocker 82.6 deg, the rod 5.58 mm for 4.6 mm needed). The link line passes on the stop side of the crank axis (by 0.277 mm closed, 0.422 mm open): any load that tries to change the state pushes the crank into its stop; a load in the other sense pulls the crank 10 deg back to the dead centre (pin moves 0.04 mm) where the state still holds, and a later reversal there needs pin friction mu_j of at least 0.10 (closed) to 0.14 (open) for an assumed 0.05 mm play. With ISO 2768-1 class f the worst-case margin past the dead centre is at least 5.19 deg (all coordinates +-0.1 bound) and 5.64 deg (size rule). Roll lock: peg hex enclosed over 1.4 mm by the jaw (upper three flats) and the flat seat, 4.10 mm across flats, 0.05 mm per side, free roll +-2.58 deg. Nothing is powered to hold.

release.means: The unit's own keeper motor M3 (Precision Microdrives 206-109 via driver-2) drives the crank over the dead centres: 203 deg from the closed stop to the open stop, retracting the tongue by 5.58 mm (4.6 mm needed with the tongue closing at z 0.0; open lower edge >= 4.6). The open state is held geometrically by the second stop. Release torque: with tongue friction at the full design tension (steel on steel, mu bound 1.0, provisional) the design tension is 4 mu W = 1.637 N for the declared 41.741 g mass and the peak crank torque over the stroke is 1.637 N x 2.871 mm = 4.70 mN m against M3 rated 3 mN m (0.64x of the requirement) and stall 9 mN m (1.91x). Release under the full mu = 1 bound tension therefore needs more than the rated torque (rated covers tongue friction up to 1.04 N, 64% of the bound); release is specified at low tension (the controller relaxes the tension first, chain yaw 0). Docking sequence: open keeper (M3), roll in, IMU detects landing, close keeper (M3). It acts only on this unit's own receiver. Crank stop wear, M3 heat and cycle life are UNRESOLVED.

alignment.description: Roll-in channel from the corrected roll kinematics: two circular-arc slots, radius 25.5 mm, centred on the two F3 bottom vertices (+-12.75, +22.084), running from the vertices to the face centre (a V opening toward +z), 5.8 mm wide, 7.0 mm deep from the tail face, 45 deg x 1.5 mm flared mouths; end plate b slot +-4.545 x +-2.6 mm at the centre.
alignment.justification: Verified with the table-height condition (world frame, A fixed, B resting on F3 and rolling from one step to the side about the shared bottom edge P): the peg point lies in B's frame on the circle of radius 25.5 about B's bottom vertex, from B's other bottom vertex to the face centre; B's lowest vertex stays on the table, its centre rises to 25.5 mm at 30 deg of roll; the peg hex turns 60 deg relative to B (hex symmetry). The final approach is along 30 deg from the body x axis (nearly sideways), not from the vertical. Slot width 5.8 mm (4.619 + 2 x 0.59) gives 0.59 mm per side nominal; SLS accuracy +-0.3% with a lower limit of +-0.3 mm (Materialise PA12 SLS, https://www.materialise.com/en/industrial/3d-printing-materials/pa12-sls) gives a minimum width 5.5 mm and 0.44 mm per side. Windows: lateral at the mouth +-(0.59+1.5) = +-2.09 mm (min +-1.94); height +-0.59 (min +-0.44); heading (two-point jam, engagement 6.5 mm) 11.3 deg nominal, 8.2 deg at the SLS minimum slot and 7.6 deg with the peg at the class-f upper limit; roll any multiple of 60 deg; axial +-0.5 mm (groove play +-0.2 plus slot play +-0.3). THERE IS NO AXIAL OR HEADING PRE-ALIGNMENT MEANS other than these windows, and a free approach cannot start a roll-in: docking needs B one roll step to the side in a common lane on the face adjacent to F3 (axial inside +-0.5 mm, heading inside the window, the peg already engaged 6.5 mm), which is only reachable by rolling out of a previous dock. After docking the relative roll is 0 (B ends on F3) and the 60 deg relative turn during entry is absorbed by the hex symmetry. Nominal geometric estimates; the capture window is not claimed (CPL-006). No magnet and no cone.

alignment.description: Tongue seating feature (not a pre-alignment means): semicircular notch r 1.55 with a 30 deg half-angle lead-in wedge (0.3 mm each side, tip face 0.4 mm) that seats the groove root as the crank closes.
alignment.justification: The V-notch of v3 is dropped as a declared pre-alignment means: with flank friction 0.15 the lateral push fraction is 0.393 (it is negative at flank friction 1), so the rated closing force 1.04 N gives 0.41 N against the neighbour's full-weight drag mu W = 0.409 N at mu 1: a ratio of 1.00 (stall 3.01), below the 1.5 rule. The notch seats a peg already inside the +-0.44 mm channel window; axial capture +-0.5 mm. The tongue is driven by M3 through the four-bar, not by a spring.

alignment.description: Hex peg on a flat seat under a three-flat jaw, with a 0.5 x 45 deg tip chamfer on the peg.
alignment.justification: The hexagonal peg (4.0 mm across flats) has six equivalent roll positions; the receiver cannot be a closed lower half-hex cup: both slanted side walls of such a cup lie entirely inside the peg's swept volume along the corrected arrival (0.60 mm penetration over the 0.6 mm wall), so only the flat bottom seat (top 0.05 mm below the peg flat) exists below the peg and the jaw closes the upper flats (30, 90, 150 deg) from above after landing. The jaw and the keeper tongue stay out of the swept peg when open: clearance to the rotating hex 0.449 mm (jaw) and 1.026 mm (tongue) at the nominal stroke, 0.58 to 0.65 mm for the tongue at the class-f stroke corners. Free roll +-2.58 deg. Torsion is carried by the top flat (jaw) and bottom flat (seat) corner contacts as a pure couple with arm 1.063 mm: 2.45 N per contact for one idle neighbour tipped (5.22 mN m) and 4.91 N for two (10.44 mN m); with the pitch couple (W/2 x 36 = 7.37 N mm over 1.4 mm = 5.26 N) the tongue-axis force is up to 10.17 N, carried by the over-centre stop. No attractive force acts: a unit that is not driven does not self-dock.

limitations: Roll-in docking was checked on paper only (kinematics re-derived with the table-height condition and a swept-volume check); the dynamics (impact, whether the ring-driven roll lands inside the windows) and the capture window are UNRESOLVED and belong to later gates. There is no axial or heading pre-alignment means, and a free approach cannot start a roll-in.
No steering or axial locomotion is provided: the body rolls only perpendicular to its axis.

Yaw bending works only while the chain rests on a face with a vertical yaw axis. Yaw torque margin at table mu = 1 is 0.96 at rated motor torque for the declared 41.741 g mass (27 T sector unchanged): bending at rated torque holds only for table mu <= about 0.96. The worm self-locks only if the worm/sector friction coefficient is at least 0.125 (UNRESOLVED).

Release under the full mu = 1 design tension needs more than the rated M3 torque (rated 0.64x, stall 1.91x); release is specified at low tension. Rod stroke 5.58 mm nominal; at the class-f corners 5.04 to 6.11 mm, which meets the 4.6 mm requirement of the z 0.0 tongue closing but not the 5.4 mm floor set for the old z -1.0 closing. Pin and yoke-bar envelope corners exceed the r <= 20 packing rule by about 0.02 mm nominal (physical outer point 19.96 mm) and by about 0.2 mm at the stroke corners (N = 25 sector would remove it).

Load reversal of the over-centre lock: the lock is passive for single-sign loads and for any load that tries to change the state; if a load pushes the crank to the dead centre (0.04 mm of pin travel) and then reverses, the dead centre is an unstable equilibrium and holds only with pin friction mu_j >= 0.10 to 0.14 (derived bound for an assumed 0.05 mm play; real friction not cited). M3 radial load = link force, up to 11.0 N (open) and 16.8 N (closed) at the combined tongue force 10.2 N; outrigger bushing pressure (d 2.0 x L 1.3) 4.3 and 6.5 MPa taking the whole link force, no PA12 bearing allowable cited (UNRESOLVED). The M2 worm shaft has no outrigger (the worm is 4.7 mm from the channel).

Thrust washer: declared as the flat thrust face of the puck, 7.6 mm2 of bearing on the cap strips. The yaw rotation (+-15 deg about z) against a y-normal face tilts a flat face; the kinematic compatibility of the flat washer with the rotating puck is UNRESOLVED. The puck-to-yaw-shaft joint, the cap bore and the cut of end plate b into three pieces are not designed.

Many masses are upper bounds from solid volumes (walls, end plates, caps, puck, peg, lobe, gear band); end plate b is the full hexagon although the V cut and slot remove material; the placement of screws and harness is a lumped stand-in; boxes of the link, rocker, rod and yoke are envelopes of swept parts; the M3 shaft stub is not boxed. Hertz contact stress at the peg corners on the 304 flats with an assumed 0.1 mm edge radius exceeds the first-yield rule of thumb (local indentation expected); the torsion contacts are the top-flat/bottom-flat pair, as in v3.

Gear teeth are integer: ring 133 T pitch r 19.95 (304 band) and pinion 14 T pitch r 2.1 (module 0.3, centre distance 17.85); spurs 41 T and 16 T at module 0.2 (centre distance 5.70); yaw worm 1 start into 27 teeth per turn at module 0.3. Tooth strength, backlash, profile and contact ratio are not assessed. No PA12 gear teeth remain. The M1 group is rotated 60 deg about the ring axis from its v3 position; the lobe analysis was redone for the new centre of mass.

Tolerances: SLS PA12 accuracy is cited from Materialise (https://www.materialise.com/en/industrial/3d-printing-materials/pa12-sls) as +-0.3% with a lower limit of +-0.3 mm and minimum wall 1 mm; machined 304 parts are specified ISO 2768-1 class f (https://amesweb.info/fits-tolerances/iso-2768-linear-dimensions-tolerances.aspx), +-0.05 mm for 0.5 to 6 mm and +-0.1 mm for 6 to 30 mm. Materialise is a service-provider page, not EOS PA 2200 material data. PA12 strength is not assessed beyond the coupler checks; heat is not assessed.

The Precision Microdrives 206-109 datasheet is headed as a sampling/target specification; the three motors run from 3.7 V by PWM limited to 3.0 V effective, a control constraint. The datasheet gives no radial shaft load rating, which the crank link and the worm load.

The QT Py regulator is rated 600 mA peak; the 2220 mW term is a bound; later board revisions may use a different regulator. The board has no LiPo charger, and regulator dropout limits use near the end of charge.

Vendor product pages (Grepow, Adafruit, Pololu, Materialise, amesweb) are classed datasheet because the schema allows only datasheet or publication. Cited values were read on 2026-11-06 and are checked by sampling at the gate record; the ATI 304 sheet cited for the thrust washer and the new 304 parts is the same document read on 2026-11-06.
A2 screws are costed at 304 density (assumption).
Only two axial couplers are declared; no lateral side-face couplers, no branching or lattices. No through-coupler data or power contacts; power transfer is not provided.
